answer: The BLIS configuration space's Pareto front has 35 distinct objective-value points across 1800 total configs. TP (tensor parallelism) is the dominant knob for throughput (scaling from 7 rps at tp=1 to 32 rps at tp=8), while num_instances controls the saturation boundary. Block_size=32 is almost universally Pareto-dominant over 16. Scheduler (fcfs vs sjf) and max_num_running_reqs matter only in the saturated regime and produce minor differences. The front is structured by GPU-count tiers: within each tier, the tradeoff is between throughput/latency and KV cache cost. A structured search algorithm that tests all single-instance combos with 2 schedulers x 2 mrr values x 6 kvb values (at bst=32), plus multi-instance combos with a smaller grid, recovers 100% of the true Pareto front using only 200 evaluations (11.1% of the full space).
